purpose: Determine whether the observed aggregate private non-financial credit transaction flow can be mapped directly into a combined private_demand_and_investment node without a purpose-, sector- and expenditure-boundary bridge.

ecb_bls.finding: Loan demand is reported separately by borrower and purpose. Corporate financing needs include fixed investment, inventories and working capital, debt refinancing/restructuring and other financing needs; household lending distinguishes house purchase from consumer credit and other lending.
ecb_bls.implication: Observed aggregate credit flow cannot be allocated one-to-one to current consumption or fixed investment.

ecb_safe.source: Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises
ecb_safe.finding: Firms report external financing used for multiple purposes, including inventories/working capital and fixed investment.
ecb_safe.implication: NFC borrowing is not definitionally equivalent to NFC gross fixed capital formation.

eurostat_consumption.finding: Household final consumption expenditure is expenditure on goods and services for direct satisfaction of needs or wants.
eurostat_consumption.implication: A financial loan transaction is a financing transaction, not household final consumption expenditure by definition.

retained_rmd.finding: RMD retains aggregate S11 plus S14/S15 loan transactions but household consumption and NFC investment are distinct sectoral national-account targets with their own unresolved behavioural/source boundaries.

structural_interpretation.credit_flow_role: Observed ECB BSI net financial transaction for domestic NFC plus household/NPISH loans.
structural_interpretation.private_demand_and_investment_role: Qualitative umbrella combining household consumption/demand and corporate investment/expenditure concepts that are measured in national accounts rather than as loan transactions.
structural_interpretation.mapping_requirement: Any quantitative credit-to-expenditure bridge requires an ex ante sector- and purpose-specific measurement contract that distinguishes house purchase, consumer credit, working capital, refinancing and fixed-investment finance, and aligns them to the chosen national-accounts expenditure target.
